basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 18-22.' and it opens 'VERS. 18-22.-- Porro Henoch genuit Irat, et reliqua usque: et Mathusalem genuit Lamech,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 18-22.-- Porro Henoch genuit Irat, et reliqua usque: et Mathusalem genuit Lamech, qui accepit | uxores duas, nomen uni Ada, et nomen alteri Sella. Lamech quippe interpretatur percutiens. Ipse percussit et interfecit Cain. Et ipse primus adulterium commisit, eo quod se in duabus uxoribus divisit. Hic notandum est quod in progenie Seth nulla ibi progenita femina nominatim exprimitur, nisi tantum in progenie Cain commemoratur; per quod significatur terrenam civitatem, qua [ Z., quae] Cain cepit [ Petr., concepit], usque sui in finem carnales habituram generationes, quae marium ac feminarum conjunctione proveniunt [ Z., quae per maritorum ac feminarum conjunctiones perveniunt]. Unde ad testimonium Sella umbra ejus interpretatur.
